A1.justification: Both 29-page PDFs present the same RoMAE research, with readable text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–D. No material gaps prevent comparison.

before.justification: V2 reports original RoMAE experiments on position reconstruction, image and audio classification, irregular time-series tasks, and supplementary analyses in Appendix B.

after.justification: V3 retains these original experiments and reports additional ELAsTiCC results using the alert mask in Table 4.

M1.justification: Sections 3–4 and Appendix A retain the same patchification, continuous axial RoPE, encoder-decoder architecture, learned tokens, and prediction heads. The ELAsTiCC revisions concern experimental settings.

E1.justification: The same datasets, populations, and tasks are retained, including the appendix experiments. The added alert-mask comparison varies preprocessing within the existing ELAsTiCC classification benchmark.

E2.justification: Table 4 retains Transformer and ATAT as comparators. Comparator membership in the other main-text and appendix comparisons is also unchanged; the added RoMAE rows are alert-mask variants.

E3.justification: Section 5.4 revises the stated ELAsTiCC pretraining mask ratio from 75% to 50% and adds evaluation with the alert mask. The 200 pretraining and 25 fine-tuning epochs remain unchanged. The PDFs do not establish whether retained results were rerun.

E4.justification: Table 4 adds a with/without-alert-mask comparison for both RoMAE sizes, testing whether discarding saturated or high-error observations helps classification. Existing positional, computational, frequency-retention, and interpolation analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Run and seed counts, standard-deviation reporting, and other uncertainty practices are unchanged. The added ELAsTiCC entries are point estimates, following the earlier Table 4 format.

E6.justification: Table 4 adds masked F-scores of 0.6649 for RoMAE-tiny-shallow and 0.7205 for RoMAE-tiny, retaining their earlier scores of 0.7106 and 0.8029 as unmasked results. Against unchanged masked ATAT at 0.6270, the new masked margins are 0.0379 and 0.0935. Other reported results are unchanged.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, propositions, corollaries, equations, and Appendix C proof are unchanged. Section 5.2 corrects a reference from Proposition 4.1 to Corollary 4.1 without revising the theory.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about RoMAE's versatility, continuous positional encoding, absolute-position recovery through learned tokens, and competitive performance across modalities.

C2.justification: Section 5.4 newly interprets stronger unmasked performance as suggesting that alert-rejected observations may contain useful information and should perhaps be retained. Existing explanations involving pretraining and model size, and the stated limitations, remain.

D1.justification: Appendix A.2 clarifies that mixed precision was exploratory and all final results use FP32, consistent with existing hyperparameter tables. Appendix D.6 newly explains alert-mask filtering and clarifies that the stated flux range refers to standardized values.

R1.justification: The cited works and substantive positioning relative to prior research are retained. The related-work discussion and reference list contain no substantive additions or removals.

P1.justification: V3 makes scattered grammar, terminology, and cross-reference corrections, locally expands the ELAsTiCC explanation, and revises the funding acknowledgment. The overall narrative and section organization remain substantially unchanged.

P2.justification: Table 4 gains an alert-mask column and two rows, with adjusted widths for the adjacent tables. Figure 4 receives an explicit caption cross-reference, and some appendix content shifts with page reflow. All figures retain their graphical content.

improvement.justification: V3 improves the credibility of the ELAsTiCC comparison by exposing differing alert-mask conditions and adding RoMAE results using the same mask as the baselines. This supports smaller, better-controlled performance margins. Clarified training and precision reporting also improves reproducibility. These are useful, localized improvements to an otherwise largely unchanged paper.
